newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industry output rebounds in November.
newsitem.headline: German industry output rebounds in November.

text.p: German industrial production rose by 1.6 percent in November, according to data released Friday by the Economics Ministry, which also revised October's output downward by over half to 0.7 percent.
Compared with the previous year, November output was up 1.3 percent after a 0.9 percent gain in October, the seasonally adjusted preliminary data showed.
The growth of industrial output in November, breaking a two-month downturn, put the economy back on course to hit modest 1996 growth targets ahead of an expected slack first quarter, analysts said.
The gain exceeded market expectations and eased fears among economists that Germany would miss a modest overall target of 1.5 percent growth in gross domestic product for 1996.
"The production rise was to be expected given the rise in orders in October. It doesn't change our forecast that German GDP rose 1.5 percent in 1996," said Uwe Angenendt at BHF-Bank.
On a quarterly basis, economists said they expected fourth quarter GDP to be stagnant or slightly higher after strong second and third quarter growth.
